# An issue link DELETED in Jira is never removed from the local ticket (inbound)

Found while writing the row-11 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table
(story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a
product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under
epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism

The inbound link differ is ADD-ONLY, by construction and by its own docstring.
`inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` opens with "Reflect Jira issuelinks into rebar
relations. ADD-only." and closes with "ADD-only (no REMOVE mutations)"
(src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py:380 and :396). It iterates
the CURRENT `fields.issuelinks` and emits an add per unseen link; nothing walks the
local deps looking for one whose Jira counterpart has gone.

So the flow is asymmetric: the OUTBOUND direction does have a removal path
(`outbound_links._diff_link_removals`, which emits
`{"action": "remove", "type":..., "to_key":..., "relation":...}`,
outbound_links.py:120-175, applied via `delete_issue_link`), while the inbound
direction has no counterpart. A link a human deletes in Jira stays on the rebar
ticket forever, and no pass ever reports it.

## Why this is a gap and not merely a documented design choice

Story 5200's acceptance criteria define a 14-row mutation table with an explicit
oracle per direction. Row 11's INBOUND oracle is "that link is ABSENT" from the
local ticket. That row cannot pass while the differ is add-only, so the epic's
comprehensiveness claim is not reachable without either implementing the removal
or amending the AC. This ticket IMPLEMENTS THE REMOVAL; the Approach below resolves
the evidence question (how we know the peer deleted a link rather than that we failed
to observe it), which is the part that made this more than a guard removal.

Note the add-only choice is not obviously safe either: the same docstring's
idempotency logic already skips an emit when "the counterpart is absent from the
ACTIVE local set", i.e. the differ is willing to reason about absence — just not
about the absence of the LINK.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips`
asserts the local dep is gone after the Jira link is deleted. It should go RED on
the harness until this is addressed.

## Approach

Mirror the outbound removal path, but gate it — an inbound removal is a WRITE that destroys local
data, so the whole design problem is establishing that the peer really DELETED the link rather than
that we merely failed to see it.

1. **A new `_diff_link_removals_inbound` in `inbound_differ.py`**, the mirror of
   `outbound_links._diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:120-175). It walks the local `deps` and
   emits `{"action": "remove", "target_id": <local id>, "relation": <local relation>}` — inbound
   records carry `target_id` (a local id), not `to_key`. Build the OBSERVED peer link set through
   `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link`, NOT from raw Jira keys, so both sides are compared in local
   relation vocabulary; comparing raw keys makes an `inwardIssue`/`Blocks` link read as `depends_on`
   while the local dep is `blocks`, producing a spurious removal of a link that is still there.

2. **`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` must branch on `action`.** It currently reads
   `if entry.get("action") != "add": continue` (apply_inbound_records.py:560-562) and only ever calls
   `rebar.link`, so a removal record is silently discarded — a differ-only fix would ship the exact
   silent-failure class this epic exists to end. Removal applies via `rebar.unlink`.

### The five guards, and why each is load-bearing

- **G1 OBSERVED.** Emit only when `"issuelinks" in jira_fields` — key PRESENT, empty list allowed.
  `fetcher.py:592-596` sets that key only for entries `get_issuelinks_map` returned a list for, and the
  base search omits issuelinks entirely (bug 3f04), so key-presence is a reliable "enrichment reached
  this issue" marker. Both readers make an empty list authoritative rather than dropping the key
  (Cloud `acli_graph.get_issuelinks_map` records `result[key] = links` for any list "including the
  empty list — an authoritative 'no links'"; DC `transport.py:391-394` builds `{key: list(... or [])}`).
  `_snapshot_schema.py` is `total=False` and never injects `[]`. So key-absent covers exactly the
  unsafe cases — enrichment failed, HTTP 410, a fail-open partial map, the issue fell outside a
  truncated page, a cross-project bound issue, or a client with no `get_issuelinks_map` — and every one
  of those fails safe to NO REMOVAL.
  **`_diff_links_inbound:397` opens `jira_fields.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses
  observed-empty into unobserved. That line must NOT be reused on the removal path.**
- **G2 TARGET BOUND.** Require `binding_store.get_jira_key(target_id)` non-None. An unbound target
  could never have had a Jira link, so its absence proves nothing.
- **G3 MANAGED.** `should_propagate_removal(relation, target_id, local_ticket)` from
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs` — the same predicate the outbound parent/link gates consume, so a
  peer-created dep rebar never owned is not clobbered. It also excludes
  `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`discovered_from` for free, because `MANAGED_REF_KINDS` omits relations
  with no reliable peer link type; do NOT add a redundant filter for them.
- **G4 ARBITRATION — REWRITTEN AFTER THE LIVE ORACLE REFUTED THE FIRST VERSION. READ THIS CAREFULLY.**
  The FIRST version of this guard said: "never mirror a removal for a target the outbound side is adding
  this pass", on the reasoning that an outbound ADD means "being pushed" rather than "peer deleted it".
  **That reasoning is WRONG, and its failure is total.** When the peer deletes a link, the local dep still
  exists and the peer lacks it — which is EXACTLY the condition under which the outbound differ emits a
  link ADD. So on any bidirectional pass a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that target,
  and the guard therefore always suppressed the inbound REMOVE: **the feature could never fire.** Proven by
  harness run 30784592232 against main @ `de2f1ed87` (which CONTAINS change 1276):
  `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` stayed RED with "the Jira link was DELETED … but the local dep …
  still targets 'jira-rbjflfv-2'". The mutation ledger was green throughout, because
  `test_g4_outbound_add_this_pass_suppresses_the_removal` asserted the behaviour the plan specified — **a
  mutation ledger cannot catch a wrong SPECIFICATION.**

  **THE CORRECTED RULE: `managed_refs` decides PRECEDENCE between the two directions. It is not a second
  AND-gate beside G3.** The two differs disagree about one fact — local dep present, peer link absent — and
  exactly one must win:
    * ref **IS managed** (rebar pushed it at some point) + peer lacks it → **the peer DELETED it** → the
      inbound REMOVE wins, **and the outbound ADD for that pair must be suppressed.**
    * ref is **NOT managed** (never pushed) + peer lacks it → **we simply have not pushed it yet** → the
      outbound ADD wins and the inbound REMOVE is suppressed. This is the ONLY case the old G4 should have
      covered.
  Suppressing only the inbound side is NOT sufficient and must not be shipped: both differs run against
  the same pre-pass snapshot and then both apply, so inbound unlinking locally while outbound re-adds in
  Jira leaves the pass DIVERGENT and the next pass re-adopts the link inbound — churn, not convergence.
  **So `outbound_links.py` (or the shared suppression context) is in scope: this is arbitration across BOTH
  differs.**
  An outbound REMOVE for the same pair still suppresses the inbound removal (the two directions must not
  both act on one pair in a pass; deferring re-evaluates next pass rather than double-removing).
- **G5 RELATION MATCH AT APPLY.** `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` takes NO relation
  argument, and that is deliberate — `_commands/unlink.py`'s usage text says "pair-scoped, NO relation
  arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and `_get_link_info` returns the most recent
  net-active link. So if a pair holds two active relations and the peer dropped only one, a naive
  unlink can remove THE WRONG ONE — a link the peer still has. The apply step must confirm the pair's
  net-active relation MATCHES the vanished relation, and skip + log otherwise.

### G3's blind spot, stated plainly rather than papered over

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the **LINK-event** processor (`reducer/_processors.py:411`), so a ref
becomes "managed" the instant it is created LOCALLY — it does NOT mean "we pushed it to the peer".
`seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for pre-feature tickets by seeding all current `deps`
as managed. So G3 alone does not establish that the peer ever had the link. **Under the CORRECTED arbitration rule above, that is handled by precedence rather than by a second gate:** an UNMANAGED dep is never removed (the outbound ADD wins), so a brand-new local dep is safe by construction. What remains is the narrower case where `managed_refs` says managed but the ref was never actually pushed — chiefly `seed_managed_refs_from_current`, which marks a PRE-FEATURE ticket's CURRENT deps as managed. On such a ticket a never-pushed dep could be read as "the peer deleted it" and removed locally. That window is real and is recorded here deliberately; it is far narrower than the behaviour it replaces, which was that the feature never fired at all.

**The earlier text here claimed "G4 closes that in a healthy pass, because outbound emits a link ADD for exactly that dep and the suppression drops the removal." That sentence was the error** — it is precisely why the first implementation could never work, and it is retained in this form only so the mistake is legible rather than quietly overwritten.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer link set** (link present in the prior Jira
snapshot, absent now = a real remote deletion). This is the textbook-correct signal and would retire
G3's blind spot outright, but it is NOT available: as of `6cdd4b00d9` ("Narrow persisted Jira snapshot
to key membership") `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set` persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership
only, carrying no fields and therefore no issuelinks. Reaching for it means adding a new persisted
artifact with its own migration and its own truncation semantics, which is a materially larger change
than this defect warrants. Recorded so a future reader knows it was considered and why it was declined.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — the removal differ + G1/G2/G3, and making
  G4 deliberate. 718/800 LOC today; a ~50-line mirror lands ~770. If it would breach 800, shed weight
  into `link_direction.py` (59 LOC, already imported by both directions), never mechanically.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — action branch + `rebar.unlink` + G5.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py` (or the shared same-pass suppression context) —
  **ADDED after the live refutation:** the managed case must also suppress the OUTBOUND link ADD, or the
  pass ends divergent and churns. This is the arbitration half the original plan did not contemplate.
  579/800 LOC.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` — OPTIONAL, only to add a `should_mirror_peer_removal` sibling
  sharing the `managed_ref_set()` read path. Mechanically the identical predicate, so it buys naming
  and a place to document that inbound needs more than the managed check. Skip it if the guards read
  clearly without it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** any fetcher or adapter change (the observed/unobserved distinction already
  survives); `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`, which another ticket owns.

## Acceptance criteria

**AMENDED after an operator ruling — see the AC AMENDMENT comment on this ticket for the full
reasoning and the ecosystem research with sources.** The ruling was: research the ecosystem, build
if it is a parity gap, defer if it is not commonly handled. It is NOT commonly handled (Aha! refuses
deletion propagation outright citing inadvertent-data-loss risk; Asana<->Jira and Workfront<->Jira
leave the far item in place; Exalate makes link sync opt-in scripted config), and it is NOT a
Cloud/DC parity gap (shared core; Cloud never mirrored a peer deletion and has no equivalent cell).
So removal-mirroring is DEFERRED and the criteria written around "the removal IS emitted" no longer
describe what this ticket ships.

The original criteria are preserved verbatim below under RETIRED rather than deleted, so the
decision is auditable.

### What this ticket actually shipped — the criteria that stand

- [x] the apply-layer DROP is fixed. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` used to
      discard any non-`add` link record outright (`action != "add": continue`), so even a correct
      differ could not have worked. That branch + the `rebar.unlink` wiring landed in change 1276
      and is independently mutation-proven. This was a REAL defect and it is fixed
- [x] G1/G2/G3/G5 landed and are mutation-proven. They are dormant (nothing emits a removal for
      them to gate) but they are correct, and they are the guards a future implementation needs
- [x] the shipped semantics are STATED: local-wins-and-restore. A link deleted in Jira is re-added
      on the next pass — convergent, no local data destroyed, identical on both backends
- [ ] the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is XFAIL with the full reason in the
      marker, `strict=False` so it fails LOUDLY as an xpass the moment a removal path starts
      working — NOT inverted and NOT deleted (Gerrit change 1303)
- [x] the ecosystem evidence is recorded, with sources, so this is not re-litigated from scratch
- [x] the refutation of the original design is recorded, with a probe — `managed_refs` cannot
      distinguish "a link we never pushed" from "a link the peer deleted"; the two states are
      IDENTICAL on every input the guards read. That finding stopped a second data-loss defect
      before it was written
- [x] the correct design is recorded WITH A WORKING TEMPLATE — change 1296 landed exactly this
      pattern for parents (a per-binding record of what the peer last had, advanced only on
      OBSERVATION), so whoever picks this up starts from shipped, reviewed code rather than from
      the refuted premise. `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs
- [x] `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap

### RETIRED — specify a feature deliberately NOT shipped

Recorded, not silently dropped. Every item below described emitting or gating a link REMOVAL, which
this ticket no longer ships. The live cell still EXISTS and still RUNS (as an xfail); what changed
is the product decision about what behaviour to ship, taken on ecosystem evidence plus a first-hand
incident in which the identical inference destroyed 63 parent edges.

- ~~RETIRED~~ a link deleted in Jira is mirrored locally: the local dep is asserted POSITIVELY ABSENT after
      the pass, never "no exception was raised"
- ~~RETIRED~~ the removal record survives the apply layer end to end — differ emit → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → `rebar.unlink` → the dep is gone from the reduced ticket. A test that stops at
      the differ boundary does NOT satisfy this, because the record was silently dropped at
      `apply_inbound_records.py:560-562` and a differ-only oracle goes green while the store is untouched
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with the issue's `issuelinks` key ABSENT (unobserved — simulate the real truncation/fail-open
      shape, not a hand-deleted key if the real path differs), NO removal is emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G1: with `issuelinks` present and EMPTY (authoritative "no links"), the removal IS emitted
- ~~RETIRED~~ G2: an unbound target emits no removal
- ~~RETIRED~~ G3: a dep that is not in `managed_refs` emits no removal, so a peer-created dep is never clobbered
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, MANAGED case: a MANAGED dep whose peer link is gone emits the removal **even
      though the outbound side is adding that target this pass**, and the outbound ADD for that pair is
      SUPPRESSED. Assert BOTH halves — inbound removal present AND outbound add absent — because
      suppressing only one leaves the pass divergent and churning
- ~~RETIRED~~ G4 arbitration, UNMANAGED case: an UNMANAGED dep whose peer link is absent emits NO removal and the
      outbound ADD proceeds, asserted against `link_add_keys`
- ~~RETIRED~~ a test pins that the two arbitration branches are decided by `managed_refs` and NOT by the mere
      presence of an outbound add — i.e. flipping only the managed-ness of the ref flips which direction
      wins. This is the assertion whose absence let the first version ship broken
- ~~RETIRED~~ the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is GREEN on a harness run, and the run id is
      recorded here. **A green unit suite is explicitly NOT sufficient for this ticket** — the first
      version had a fully green, mutation-checked unit suite and did not work at all
- ~~RETIRED~~ G5: when the pair's net-active relation differs from the vanished relation, no unlink is
      performed and the skip is logged
- ~~RETIRED~~ steady state does not churn: a managed dep still present on the peer emits NO removal on
      repeated passes
- ~~RETIRED~~ every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the removal unconditional — a fix that emits removals with no guard passes
      the happy-path oracle while being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that
      actually protect the product
- ~~RETIRED~~ `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is
      unmodified, and turns GREEN on the harness once this lands
- ~~RETIRED~~ `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap
